Show HN: Muscle Memory – Can you still write code without AI?
item.description:
Developer of 6 years here, been using AI (increasingly) over the last year for most of my work. A few weeks back I started to look for new jobs as the current startup I work for is falling into pieces. "Do I need to do leetcode again?" - I thought. So I picked a few challenges and tried to solve them without an assistant.

This felt impossible. What?! Is this the brainrot everyone is talking about? I mean I still read code every day, I just don't write it anymore. I could read and review the solution easily, but writing it myself felt like speaking a language I only understand, but cannot speak.

Being the data hoarder I am, I immediately wanted numbers, so I built Muscle Memory to help me feed them.

It's like leetcode but better. Challenges are more realistic, and I'd like to think the UX is more straightforward. It covers 12 languages and your code runs in a network-denied sandbox in your browser. No account needed.

I want it to be a place to keep your hands sharp: short tasks, clear prompts, and difficulty that comes from solving the problem rather than figuring out what the question means.

About the data (that I'm curious about): With your consent, Muscle Memory records your practice as raw events, including keystrokes, runs and submissions. Hoping to build an open dataset of how we write code in the AI era. That could help us understand how we approach problems, where we get stuck, and how we well do we retain our craft during this transition.

Your individual results stay private unless you share them. “Stealth” mode keeps your data out of published findings, and you can export or delete everything.

The data will be published as a report/notebook on the site itself, and be available raw under MIT license (parquet) once we reach a critical mass of sorts, so it makes sense to share.

The code is also MIT-licensed on GitHub (https://github.com/ekkuleivonen/muscle-memory). I wrote more about why I built it in the manifesto here: https://musclememory.run/manifesto.

I'd especially like to hear what surprised you about your first attempt.

Try it out here: https://musclememory.run

Show HN: Coding agent spots your AI practices and the ones you're missing
item.description:
Frontier models improve at a pace faster than the pace at which most humans are able to keep up. Not all of us are obsessed with pushing the boundaries of our agents and trying new ways to work with them. I often spend 12+ hours a day working with an LLM, and still, when I talk to people, I hear of ways of working I hadn’t thought of.

What if we could speed up that pace of learning? What if everybody shared their practices of how they are making the most of AI, and if we could learn from each other? What if AI could make that sharing happen? Could everyone catch up with AI then?

I know, it sounds dreamy, but my therapist says illusions are necessary—until some of them come true.

I built a tool that teaches your local agent to scan your sessions, spot the best practices you already use, and guide you towards the ones you haven’t discovered yet. Only names and counts reach the server. Your sessions never do.

The product has a self-consolidating catalogue of practices, MCP servers, plugins and skills.

Here’s my stack—scan (locally, all session data remains private). https://app.userrank.ai/@milstan

To spice things up and give a reason to rescan, I added rankings inspired by Foursquare (who here is old enough to remember Foursquare when it was gamified?). You can rank in the top 10 of a city, or of a field like Product.

Claude Code, 10–20 minutes on your own plan:

claude plugin marketplace add https://app.userrank.ai/plugins/marketplace.json claude plugin install userrank@userrank claude "Get my UserRank"

Codex, or a quick scan of your Claude or ChatGPT chats: https://app.userrank.ai/start
